validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification; row is a real, correctly-classified FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM. Docket CP15-514-000 (Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC 7(c) application, filed 2015-06-08; pre-filing PF14-23-000 assigned 2014-10-09); FERC approved construction 2017-01-19; in-service 2018-01-01 (TC Energy's own announcement); the pipeline suffered a landslide-caused rupture/explosion near Moundsville, Marshall County, WV on 2018-06-07 (widely reported: WV MetroNews, DeSmog, and PHMSA opened an investigation) -- a real, physically-existing, operating asset, corroborated by a federal regulatory notice (Federal Register 2015-06-29, an independent-of-operator origin) plus TC Energy's own press releases plus independent news coverage (WV MetroNews, DeSmog). CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating natural gas transmission pipeline (not a gathering/feeder line) -- it is FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission carrying Marcellus/Utica gas into the Columbia Gas Transmission system toward Southeast/Gulf Coast markets. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster -- no other row names Leach XPress or plausibly describes the same physical pipe; not a duplicate/relabel. CAVEATS folded into separate concern entries below: (1) Location (StartState/EndState) is wrong, (2) SegmentCost is very likely the combined Leach+Rayne XPress estimate mis-recorded as Leach XPress's own segment cost.

validity.recommendation: correct StartState/Province and EndState/Province to West Virginia (Marshall County origin; Wayne County terminus) -- Pennsylvania (Greene County) and Ohio (10 counties) are pass-through states on this route, not the endpoints. If the schema forces a choice of only one 'representative' pass-through state, Ohio is the better single non-WV state to keep (it carries by far the most route mileage/county count), but Pennsylvania as the START state is not supported by any source found.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently records StartState/Province=Pennsylvania, EndState/Province=Ohio. Every independent primary/secondary source found describes the opposite: the line ORIGINATES in Marshall County, West Virginia (the state's northern panhandle, near Pittsburgh, PA) and TERMINATES in Wayne County, West Virginia (the WV-KY-OH tripoint area in far southeastern Ohio's immediate vicinity) -- with Greene County, Pennsylvania and ten Ohio counties (Monroe, Noble, Muskingum, Morgan, Perry, Fairfield, Hocking, Jackson, Lawrence, Vinton) crossed in between. Four independent sources agree: (1) Columbia Pipeline Group's own 2015 project FAQ ('The Leach XPress pipeline will originate in Marshall County, West Virginia and travel through southwestern Pennsylvania and southeastern Ohio and end in Wayne County, West Virginia' -- tcenergy.com FAQ PDF, verified); (2) the Federal Register's 2015-06-29 Notice of Application for FERC Docket CP15-514-000, an independent federal-regulatory source, which states verbatim: 'Facilities to be constructed are located in Marshall and Wayne Counties, West Virginia, Greene County, Pennsylvania, and Monroe, Noble, Muskingum, Morgan, Perry Fairfield, Hocking, Jackson, Lawrence and Vinton Counties, Ohio' (fetched and confirmed directly, not just via the verifier's substring check); (3) WV MetroNews (2018-01-04), independent trade/local press, 'Begins in Marshall County, West Virginia ... crosses into Ohio ... terminates near the West Virginia-Kentucky border in southeastern Ohio'; (4) DeSmog (2018-06-07), independent press, same route description plus siting the June 2018 rupture at Nixon Ridge, Marshall County, WV. No source found supports Pennsylvania as a terminus (start or end) -- PA is crossed only briefly near the WV origin. Tier: high (4 independent sources, including one federal-regulatory origin distinct from the operator). GEM's schema records only one Start/End state pair, but the real termini are BOTH in West Virginia; flagging both cells rather than picking one arbitrarily.

validity.recommendation: revise SegmentCost toward ~$1.6 billion (TC Energy's own final, project-specific, post-completion figure) rather than $1.75 billion, which is very likely the COMBINED Leach XPress + Rayne XPress cost estimate (a companion, non-roster Gulf Coast project filed and approved in the same docket family) misattributed to Leach XPress alone.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost=1,750,000,000 USD. Every Leach-XPress-SPECIFIC cost figure found disagrees with this and clusters instead around $1.4-1.6B, while every ~$1.75-1.8B figure found is explicitly stated as the COMBINED Leach XPress + Rayne XPress total: (a) TC Energy's own 2018-01-02 in-service announcement (the most authoritative, final, project-specific figure, issued after completion): 'an investment of approximately US$1.6 billion' for Leach XPress alone (tcenergy.com, verified); (b) an independent engineering-firm case study (slidenine.com, verified, name_found) states Leach XPress's 'total cost of $1.6 billion' -- a second, independent origin agreeing with (a); (c) TC Energy's own 2017-01-19 construction-approval announcement gave an earlier, pre-completion estimate of 'approximately $1.4 billion' for Leach XPress; (d) by contrast, Marcellus Drilling News (2017-01, verified) headlines 'FERC Approves $1.8B Leach & Rayne XPress Pipeline Projects' and states this is the COMBINED figure for both projects together (citing an original August-2014 Columbia Pipeline Group estimate of $1.75B combined) -- i.e., $1.75B/$1.8B is a two-project total, not Leach XPress's own segment cost. Rayne XPress is a Gulf Coast Louisiana project, not one of this batch's 46 rows, so there is no sibling GEM row this total could correctly belong to either -- it simply should not be on P0209 as a stand-alone figure. Tier: high for the $1.6B correction (2 independent, Leach-specific sources: TC Energy's own completion release + an independent case study); the combined-cost hypothesis for the $1.75B origin is medium-confidence reasoning, stated as such.
